name: Orion
notes: One of the most recognizable constellations; best seen in winter

name: Ursa Major
notes: Contains the Big Dipper asterism; circumpolar from mid-latitudes

name: Ursa Minor
notes: Contains the Little Dipper and Polaris the North Star

name: Cassiopeia
notes: Distinctive W shape; circumpolar from northern latitudes

name: Leo
notes: Prominent spring constellation; contains bright star Regulus

name: Scorpius
notes: Vivid summer constellation; contains bright star Antares

name: Sagittarius
notes: Rich Milky Way constellation; teapot asterism points to galactic center

name: Gemini
notes: Winter constellation; contains bright stars Castor and Pollux

name: Taurus
notes: Winter constellation; contains the Pleiades and Hyades clusters

name: Boötes
notes: Spring constellation; contains bright star Arcturus

name: Cygnus
notes: Summer constellation; contains Deneb; part of the Summer Triangle

name: Lyra
notes: Small but bright; contains Vega; part of the Summer Triangle

name: Aquila
notes: Summer constellation; contains Altair; part of the Summer Triangle

name: Perseus
notes: Winter constellation; contains the Double Cluster and Algol

name: Virgo
notes: Largest zodiac constellation; contains bright star Spica

name: Hercules
notes: Summer constellation; contains the great globular cluster M13

name: Andromeda
notes: Autumn constellation; our nearest large galaxy M31 lies within it

name: Corona Borealis
notes: Small but distinctive semicircle of stars; spring/summer sky

name: Canis Major
notes: Contains Sirius the brightest star; prominent in winter

name: Big Dipper
notes: Seven-star ladle shape forming the tail of Ursa Major; pointer to Polaris

name: Little Dipper
notes: Fainter dipper shape in Ursa Minor; end star is Polaris

name: Orion's Belt
notes: Three bright stars in a row at the center of Orion: Alnitak Alnilam Mintaka

name: Summer Triangle
notes: Vega Deneb and Altair; dominates the summer and autumn night sky

name: Winter Hexagon
notes: Six bright stars forming a huge hexagon visible in winter; includes Sirius Rigel and Betelgeuse
